# 4 Ezra Chapter 9 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — Fourth vision

---

**9:1** He answered me and said: Measure carefully in your mind, and when you see that a part of the signs I spoke of have passed,

**9:2** then you will understand that it is that very time in which the Most High is about to visit the world he has made.

**9:3** And when there shall be seen in the world earthquakes among peoples, uproar of peoples, intrigues of nations, confusion of leaders, disquietude of princes —

**9:4** then you shall understand that of these things the Most High spoke from the days before you, from the beginning.

**9:5** For as all that is done in the world has a beginning and an end, so also are the appointed times of the Most High; the beginnings are manifest in wonders and mighty works, and the endings in requital and in signs.

**9:6** And it shall be that whoever shall have been saved and shall be able to escape by his works, and by the faith in which you have believed,

**9:7** shall be preserved from the aforesaid perils and shall see my salvation in my land and within my borders; for I have sanctified them for myself from the beginning.

**9:8** Then those who have now abused my ways shall be amazed, and those who have rejected them with contempt shall dwell in torments.

**9:9** For as many as in their life received benefits and did not acknowledge them; and as many as despised my law while they yet had liberty, and did not understand but despised it while repentance was yet open to them —

**9:10** these must learn it by torment after death.

**9:11** Therefore be not curious to know how the ungodly shall be punished; but inquire how the righteous shall be saved — for whose sake the world is created and the age began.

**9:12** Then I answered and said: I said it before, and I say it now, and I will say it hereafter: there are more who perish than those who shall be saved,

**9:13** as a wave is greater than a drop.

**9:14** And he answered me and said: As is the field, so also is the seed; and as are the flowers, so also are their colors; and as is the work, so also is the evaluation thereof; and as is the husbandman, so also is the threshing-floor.

**9:15** For there was a time in this age when I was preparing for those who now live, before the world was made for them to dwell in, and no one opposed me then, for no one existed.

**9:16** Now also those who are created in this world, which is supplied both with an unfailing table and an inexhaustible pasture, have corrupted themselves in their ways.

**9:17** So I looked upon my world, and behold, it was ruined; and upon my earth, and behold, it was in peril because of the devices of those who had come into it.

**9:18** And I saw and spared it hardly, and saved for myself one from many, and one from a countless multitude,

**9:19** and these are they who now rule over you, saying to themselves: We alone have obtained what no other man could obtain.

**9:20** And now I no longer rejoice over the multitude of those who have perished; for those who are now living have begun again before my face to commit the same evils as those of the first world.

**9:21** Then I answered and said: For you granted the earth Adam and your own creation; all others descended from him you have not forced to do evil, but you granted it to him by his desire; and it was not a multitude of the righteous before you, but he who was numbered among the righteous.

**9:22** Then I answered and said: I know, O LORD, that the Most High is called compassionate, because he has compassion on those who have not yet come into the world; and merciful, because he has mercy on those who return to his law;

**9:23** and long-suffering, because he bears long with those who have sinned as his own creatures;

**9:24** and bountiful, because he would rather give than take away;

**9:25** and of great compassion, because he multiplies his compassion more and more upon those living now and upon those who are past and upon those of the age to come.

**9:26** For if he should not multiply his mercy, the world and all who were created in it could not live;

**9:27** and he gives — for he is a giver — and heals — for he is a healer — and plants — for he is a planter — and cuts off — for he cuts off — and makes dry — for he makes dry — and makes to flow — for he makes to flow — and creates — for he creates — and destroys — for he destroys —

**9:28** and he guides — for he guides — and raises up — for he raises up.

**9:29** For nobody can correct what he has made, and nobody can overthrow what he has approved;

**9:30** for there is no other beside him; therefore he governs his creatures by his own wisdom, and not through any other wisdom beside his own.

**9:31** Then I answered and said: What then shall I do? For I have come to a position where I can neither praise you for these things easily, nor easily be silent about them.

**9:32** For there is no guidance for those coming into the world in the last times; but things are set before them in the present that they should observe.

**9:33** From these therefore I will not be silent, but will speak of them; but of other things I will not speak without being commanded.

**9:34** Then he said to me: I told you before, and now I say it again: go and eat of the flowers of the field; taste no flesh, and drink no wine, but eat only of the flowers;

**9:35** and pray to the Most High continually — I will come and speak with you.

**9:36** I went, as he told me, to the field called Ardat; and there I sat among the flowers and ate of the herbs of the field; and the sustenance thereof satisfied me.

**9:37** And it came to pass after seven days that I lay upon the grass, and my heart was troubled again as before;

**9:38** and I opened my mouth and began to speak before the Most High.

**9:39** And behold, there came toward me a woman, mourning and weeping with a loud voice, greatly grieved in heart; her clothes were torn, and she had ashes upon her head.

**9:40** Then I let go of the thoughts I had been thinking, and I turned to her

**9:41** and said to her: Why do you weep? And why are you grieved in your mind?

**9:42** And she said to me: Let me alone, my lord, that I may weep for myself and add to my sorrows; for I am sorely distressed in my heart, and am greatly humbled.

**9:43** And I said to her: What has happened to you? Tell me. And she said to me: I was barren and had no child, though I had a husband thirty years;

**9:44** and those thirty years I spent night and day and every hour making petition before the Most High.

**9:45** And it came to pass after thirty years that God heard me, your handmaid, and saw my low estate, and considered my distress, and gave me a son; and I was very joyful over him, I and my husband and all my neighbors; and we gave great glory to the Mighty One.

**9:46** And I nurtured him with great labor; and when he grew up and I came to take him a wife, I made him a feast day.

**9:47** And it came to pass when my son entered into his wedding chamber, he fell down and died.
